payload.clothing: Travelers in plain tunics and cloaks suited to dusty desert roads; the Samaritan wears a practical traveling cloak and carries oil and wine
payload.light: Harsh, bright sunlight on the road, softening to warm golden evening light at the inn
payload.place: Rocky, dusty Jerusalem–Jericho road in Judea, with stony hills and scattered thorn scrub, leading toward a roadside inn
payload.timeOfDay: Midday heat, shifting to late afternoon and evening at the inn
payload.weather: Clear, dry, hot sky with no rain

payload.name: the Samaritan
payload.note: Traveler in the parable who tends a robbery victim (ch. 10).

stages.label: the Samaritan

quotes.quote: a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was
He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn

stages.text: the Samaritan: adult man of middle age, sturdy and weathered build, olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cropped beard, plain lined face with steady eyes. Signature outfit worn on the road: undyed linen tunic in earth tones of ochre and brown with a dusty woollen cloak in deep blue-grey, sandals and a leather belt bearing a small pouch of coins. Carries alone a water skin and a folded cloth for binding wounds.

payload.name: Wounded traveler in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: Unnamed man inside the story Jesus tells in Luke 10:30–35, traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho, stripped, beaten and left half dead. Distinct from the framing lawyer and from the Samaritan who helps him. Injuries and lost clothing are situational, not a separate life stage.

stages.label: Wounded traveler

quotes.quote: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him
leaving him half dead.

stages.text: Wounded traveler: a man of about 30 to 45 years, of average build with a lean, weathered frame, olive skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard. Facial features are plain and worn, marked with dust and bruising. Stripped to a simple loincloth of undyed linen, he has no cloak or sandals. Signature props: none.

payload.name: Robbers in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: Unnamed group inside Jesus’s story in Luke 10:30 who attack the traveler and depart. Distinct from the men crucified with Jesus and all other robbery groups. Describe a typical member.

stages.label: Robbers (typical member)

quotes.quote: he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed

stages.text: Robbers: a typical member is a lean adult man, aged late twenties to forties, of wiry build with weathered olive skin, dark hair and short beard. He wears a faded earth-brown tunic belted at the waist with a dusty cloak of undyed wool and leather sandals. Signature props carried alone: a short knife at the belt and a rough wooden cudgel.

payload.name: Priest in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: Unnamed priest inside the narrated story in Luke 10:31, who sees the traveler and passes on the other side. Distinct from every named priest elsewhere and from the framing speakers.

stages.label: Priest in the Samaritan parable

quotes.quote: By chance a certain priest was going down that way.

stages.text: Priest in the Samaritan parable: a man of middle years with a lean, weathered build and dark, short-cropped hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey. Sun-browned skin and a serious, careful face. He wears a long priestly robe of undyed linen with a dark woven sash and a fringed prayer shawl over the shoulders, in muted ochre and off-white. He carries nothing in his hands but a small leather scrip at his side.

payload.name: Levite in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: Unnamed Levite inside the narrated story in Luke 10:32, who sees the traveler and passes on the other side. Distinct from the priest immediately before him and from named Levites elsewhere.

stages.label: Levite

quotes.quote: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.

stages.text: Levite in the Samaritan parable: an unnamed Jewish man of Levite lineage in his thirties to forties, of lean, moderate build, with olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic and a dusty brown woollen cloak with a fringed hem, belted at the waist, and carries a small leather satchel.

payload.name: Innkeeper in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: Unnamed host of the inn inside the story in Luke 10:35, entrusted with the injured traveler’s care and given two denarii. Distinct from the Samaritan, injured traveler and framing speakers.

stages.label: Innkeeper

quotes.quote: he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him

stages.text: Innkeeper: a man of middle years, forties, sturdy and weathered from the roadside trade; medium build with broad, work-worn hands; olive skin, dark hair cropped short with a close-trimmed beard shot with grey; lined, steady face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a dull brown wool cloak; earth-brown and ochre tones. Signature prop: a small leather purse at his belt holding coins.

payload.name: Samaritan’s mount in the parable
payload.note: The Samaritan’s own animal inside the story in Luke 10:34, used to carry the injured man to the inn. The text fixes ownership and use but not species, colour or markings; any chosen species/appearance is illustrative invention or tradition, not a textual claim.

stages.label: The Samaritan's mount

quotes.quote: He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

stages.text: Samaritan’s mount in the parable: a sturdy donkey of the Judean hill country with a strong back, a plain brown coat, pale muzzle and legs, and a simple worn leather saddle and harness.

payload.name: Jerusalem–Jericho road in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: The descending journey from Jerusalem to Jericho inside the narrated story in Luke 10:30–34. It is the inner story’s road, not the location of Jesus’s conversation with the lawyer. The text fixes endpoints and descending travel; specific terrain details follow the era/illustrative tradition.

stages.label: Jerusalem–Jericho road

quotes.quote: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho

stages.text: Jerusalem–Jericho road: a steep, stony track descending through the arid Judean wilderness from the hill city toward the low Jordan valley. Rocky limestone ridges and gullies line the way, with dry scrub, scattered acacia and thorn, and patches of wild grass. Rough boulders and cairns mark the path, and distant terraced hills and the faint outline of a walled town lie ahead in the desert haze.

payload.name: Inn in the Samaritan parable
payload.note: Unnamed inn inside the narrated story in Luke 10:34–35, where the Samaritan brings the injured traveler and pays the host. Distinct from the road and from the framing conversation. The text gives an inn, not a specific architectural description.

stages.label: Roadside inn

quotes.quote: brought him to an inn, and took care of him
gave them to the host

stages.text: Roadside inn: a modest two-storey inn of pale limestone blocks on the Jerusalem to Jericho road in Roman Judea, with a flat roof, a low arched gateway wide enough for a laden animal, and an open courtyard with a stone well and a water trough. Scrub and dry terraces of olive and fig stand behind it, and the rough track runs past its gate.

payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: Lawyer who tests Jesus (Luke 10)
payload.note: The unnamed expert in the law in Luke 10 who asks about inheriting eternal life and who his neighbor is; distinct from Zenas, a separate lawyer named in Titus.

stages.label: Lawyer who tests Jesus

quotes.quote: a certain lawyer stood up and tested him

stages.text: Lawyer who tests Jesus: man in his middle years, lean and watchful; olive skin, weathered by sun; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey; lined brow and keen, searching dark eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of deep blue with a fringed tallit-style prayer shawl of white and blue over the shoulders. Carries a small leather scroll case at his belt, nothing else.

payload.name: Judea (Gospel region around Jerusalem)
payload.note: The southern Jewish region around Jerusalem named in Mark and Luke, where Herod reigns and crowds come to John and Jesus; the Luke entry includes the hill country of Judea and the Roman province.

stages.label: Judea, the hill country around Jerusalem

quotes.quote: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
all these sayings were talked about throughout all the hill country of Judea.

stages.text: Judea: rolling limestone hill country of terraced slopes, dry scrub and olive groves, stone-walled fields and winding dirt roads. Villages of pale cut-stone houses with flat roofs, a few synagogues of dressed stone, and Jerusalem's walls and temple mount rising on the skyline. Stony wilderness and mountains lie east toward the Jordan valley. Olive, fig and terebinth trees, sparse grass.

payload.name: The Ancient of Days
payload.note: The divine figure on a fiery throne in Daniel's vision of the beasts; a distinct visionary figure, seen only in Daniel's dream-vision.

stages.label: The Ancient of Days

quotes.quote: His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool.
His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
A fiery stream issued and came out from before him.

stages.text: The Ancient of Days: brilliant white radiance; bright orange fire; soft white cloud; brilliant white light.

payload.name: Ministering assembly in Daniel's vision
payload.note: The unidentified assembly ministering before the Ancient of Days in Daniel 7:10; distinct from earthly Babylonian royal attendants. A group whose canon describes a typical member.

stages.label: Ministering assembly

quotes.quote: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him. Thousands of thousands ministered to him. Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The judgment was set. The books were opened.

stages.text: Ministering assembly in Daniel's vision: a typical member is an adult of medium height and slim build, with warm brown skin, dark curly hair and a short dark beard, wearing an undyed linen robe, a narrow woven belt and plain sandals.

payload.name: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)
payload.note: The Jewish youth taken captive to Babylon, renamed Belteshazzar, who interprets dreams and receives visions; the main entry with many sections in Daniel, distinguished from the prophet named only in Matthew's citation.

stages.label: Daniel (Belteshazzar), prophet of Babylon

quotes.quote: Now among these of the children of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar
he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem)

stages.text: Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man in his youth grown to a grave, graying elder; olive-brown skin; dark hair cropped close and a short trimmed beard flecked with grey; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.

aliases: one like a son of man
payload.name: One like a son of man
payload.note: The figure coming with the clouds of heaven to receive dominion in Daniel's vision; not the Gospel Jesus, but a distinct heavenly figure in Daniel.

stages.label: One like a son of man

quotes.quote: there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of Days

stages.text: One like a son of man: a man in his prime, early thirties, of athletic but dignified build; skin warm olive-brown; short dark hair and a close-cut beard; calm, steady features with a grave, luminous gaze. He wears a long white linen tunic with a deep blue-purple cloak falling from the shoulders, edged with gold thread. He carries no props.

payload.name: Babylon
payload.note: The city and empire of exile and captivity across the prophets, histories and psalms, also called Babylonia, Shinar and the land of the Chaldeans; the same place in every division.

stages.label: Babylon

quotes.quote: The wide walls of Babylon will be utterly overthrown. Her high gates will be burned with fire.
I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up.
He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who acknowledge me.

stages.text: Babylon: a vast walled city of baked brick on a flat plain watered by broad canals and rivers, its wide walls rising high and its great gates of bronze-banded cedar. Date palms and reed beds line the riverbanks, and ziggurat towers and palace roofs of brick rise above the flat skyline, with the temple of Bel among them.

sourceUnits.text: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’
Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
